context: Request: the most recent white collar matter where the client cooperated with the government, and the supporting document. Rubric: 1032-00007 (Halcyon Semiconductor) and its vsd-cover-letter-bis.docx (voluntary self-disclosure cover letter to BIS), plus a precision criterion. All runs named 1039-00005 (Torchlight Mining, FCPA/SEC investigation) instead.

first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) the review at [50] named that matter among the unopened candidates; the agent then listed other high-numbered matters and wrote its answer.

runs.failure_point: The matter it needed surfaced in its subfolder and file-name finds, but it read six other candidates and named a different investigation.

first_error.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
first_error.why: Its subfolder and file-path finds at [24]-[26] showed the matter it needed (an investigation subfolder), but the six matters it chose to read left that matter out and it never opened it.
first_error.critic_note: (generic flag) the reviews at [28] (truncated hit list) and [53] (only a subset of ~58 surfaced matters opened) flagged the gap generically, without naming that matter; the agent wrote its answer.

divergence: All three runs failed the same way at the answer (the same investigation matter named instead) but went off course at different stages. T0 surfaced the matter in its file-name search and listed its files, including the cover letter, then read five other matters (listed document not opened, [38]-[50]). T2 surfaced it in its subfolder and file-path finds but left it out of the six matters it read (surfaced, not opened, [29]-[53]). T1 never surfaced it: its scans failed or returned nothing and its file-name find was cut by its own 240-line limit (search miss, [44]-[57]). The critic flagged each gap and each was ignored: by name in T0 ([50]), the line limit in T1 ([57]), and generically in T2 ([28], [53]).
